abstract: This study examines ChatGPT adoption patterns across workers in AI-exposed occupations, finding that approximately half have used the tool but adoption is highly unequal. Women are 16 percentage points less likely to adopt ChatGPT than men, and employer restrictions significantly limit broader adoption. These disparities in AI tool access risk exacerbating existing labor market inequalities among workers.
keyFindings: Approximately 50% of workers in AI-exposed occupations have adopted ChatGPT
Women are 16 percentage points less likely to use ChatGPT compared to men
Employer restrictions on ChatGPT use hinder broader worker adoption of the tool
Unequal adoption of AI tools threatens to exacerbate existing inequalities among workers
